title: Relaxation Activities
summary:
Pregnancy brings hormonal and emotional changes that can cause stress, anxiety, insomnia, muscle tension, and fatigue. The chapter presents relaxation as an essential part of a prenatal exercise program, not an optional extra. It says these practices reduce cortisol, improve heart rate variability, lower prenatal depression and anxiety, and support the mother-baby bond and postpartum recovery.

It describes eight methods: progressive muscle relaxation, autogenic relaxation, diaphragmatic breathing, mindfulness, positive visualization of birth, massage, aquatic relaxation, and music. Each has an aim, components, and duration. A 60-min sample session and a stage-by-stage guide close the chapter, with an emphasis on a trained professional guiding the practice.
points: Relaxation lowers cortisol and adrenaline while promoting oxytocin and endorphins.
Listed benefits include lower blood pressure and heart rate, less lower back pain, better sleep, and less anxiety.
Progressive muscle relaxation (Jacobson) lasts 10-20 min, with arm tension held 5 s in a side-lying or supported seated position.
Progressive muscle relaxation is reported to significantly reduce stress and improve sleep after 8 weeks of practice.
Autogenic relaxation (Schultz) sessions run 15-25 min, with initial guided practice from a physiotherapist or psychologist.
Diaphragmatic breathing uses nasal inhalation, slow exhalation, and a rhythm of four to six breaths per minute.
Prenatal mindfulness starts with one 60-min session per week, including meditation, body scan, breathing, and visualization.
Aquatic relaxation takes place in a warm pool at 32-34 degrees C, and music should be soft (60-70 bpm) at moderate volume.
The 60-min sample session is: breathing 10 min, muscle relaxation 15, body awareness 20, light stretching 10, closing 5.
takeaways: Practice relaxation regularly, not only when stressed.
Use side-lying or supported seated positions for relaxation work.
Try slow breathing at four to six breaths per minute.
Use gentle self-massage on neck, back, and legs, with light pressure and natural oils.
Play soft music at home before bed to help sleep.
Early in pregnancy use simple breathing and brief mindfulness; later add muscle relaxation and gentle yoga; near birth add visualization, massage, and music.
cautions: In the third trimester, avoid abdominal tension or breath-holding (apnea) during muscle relaxation.
In massage, avoid deep abdominal pressure and reflex points on the ankles or wrists.
Relative contraindications include orthostatic hypotension, breathing difficulties, or emotional hypersensitivity.
